intro: Some people come to Krabi wanting to sleep right by the beach, lulled by the waves — but plenty of others are after the opposite: quiet, green trees and an easy price, then a shuttle ride down to the beach during the day · Vipa Tropical Resort plays that role well — a small bungalow resort tucked into tropical grounds below the limestone cliffs in the Ao Nang area, about 2 kilometres from Ao Nang Beach (around a 25-minute walk), with a free beach shuttle several times a day · It has 17 units/rooms, spacious bungalows that feel like having your own private house in the garden, plus a pool and a small restaurant · From around THB 1,300/night · 8.9 on Trip.com and 4.5/5 on TripAdvisor from about 250 reviews (ranked #12 of 250 B&B/Inn properties in Ao Nang)

body.html: Vipa Tropical Resort overview — who it suits — to put it as simply as possible, Vipa Tropical Resort is a stay for people who come to Krabi wanting "calm in nature" more than the convenience of being right by the beach and the shops · It is not a beachfront resort where you open the door onto sand, and it is not a hotel in the middle of Ao Nang where you step out into hundreds of bars and restaurants · Instead it is a small bungalow resort of just 17 units/rooms, tucked into tropical grounds below the limestone cliffs in the Ao Nang area, selling quiet, green trees and the feel of staying at your own private garden house · It has been open since 2007 and had a major renovation in 2010 · It is still running today and does well among small properties, scoring 8.9 on Trip.com and 4.5/5 on TripAdvisor from about 250 reviews, which puts it #12 of 250 B&B/Inn properties in Ao Nang · Real reviews line up on who fits here: couples who want a quiet, romantic feel, families who want their kids to run around the garden, and travellers who focus on relaxing and are happy to use the shuttle down to the beach — rather than people who need to step out of the room and hit the sea right away

Location and getting around — this is both the highlight and the thing you most need to understand about Vipa · The resort sits in the Ao Nang area of Mueang Krabi, but it is not beachfront — about 2 kilometres from Ao Nang Beach, or roughly a 25-minute walk, a distance that many reviews say outright is too far to walk comfortably in Krabi's heat · The good news is that the resort runs a free beach shuttle several times a day, going in and out of the Ao Nang area on a set schedule, and a lot of reviews praise it for solving the distance problem and making staying away from the beach far less of an issue than you might fear · But you do need to plan around the shuttle times, because if you miss a run you will have to call a taxi or a motorbike taxi yourself · In terms of access, the resort sits on a quiet lane surrounded by trees, so it really is calm at night with almost no noise · For longer trips: it is about 25 kilometres from Krabi Airport (KBV), or roughly a 30–40 min drive, and about 20–30 minutes into Krabi town · The resort offers a paid airport transfer, and if you are flying in it is worth booking ahead, since finding a car into the lane at night can be tricky

"It feels like escaping the chaos of Ao Nang. You wake up to limestone cliff views and birdsong, the staff help with everything, and there are several beach shuttle runs — it really is quiet and calm, but you have to like this kind of atmosphere for it to be worth it."

Room types and decor — Vipa is a small resort with about 17 units/rooms total, split into several types to suit your group size · It starts with the Standard Room, the cheapest entry-level room, good for couples or travellers who just need a place to sleep rather than spend all day in the room · Up a step is the Superior Triple Room, which sleeps 3, good for a small group of friends or a family · And the highlight most reviews talk about is the One-Bedroom Villa and Two-Bedroom Villa, separate bungalows in the garden · What guests agree they love is how much bigger the bungalows are than you would expect for the price — many use the phrase "like having your own little house in the garden," because there is plenty of living space and a private balcony to catch the breeze · Every room has air conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen TV and a private bathroom · The decor is a simple tropical-resort style in wood tones, not luxurious or modern, but it feels warm and blends into the garden · To be straight with you, some reviews mention furniture and beds in a few units that are starting to show their age, plus the odd set of sheets that look well used — understandable for a resort open since 2007, and a good reason to check the room condition at check-in and ask to switch if it is not okay

Facilities and the pool — the heart of Vipa is the shady green tropical garden with the limestone cliffs as a backdrop, which almost every review names as the thing they remember · Walking through the resort feels like being in a small forest, with big shade trees and birdsong · In the middle is an outdoor pool ringed by trees and mountain views, better for a cooling dip after a day at sea than a big pool for serious laps · The area around the pool is quiet and private because the resort is small and never crowded · There is also free Wi-Fi, free parking and a tour desk for diving, horse riding and sea activities arranged through the resort · But to be honest, being a small property, the facilities are limited compared with a big hotel — there is no 24-hour front desk, no gym, and some rooms have no safe · Another thing many reviews mention is Wi-Fi that is slow or unstable at times, especially in the bungalows deeper in the garden · If you need to work online seriously or take video calls, bring a mobile data SIM as a backup plan

Food and dining — the resort has a small on-site restaurant serving both Thai food and simple dishes, with room service · Breakfast is available, but this is where reviews are fairly mixed — some say the breakfast is plain with not many choices and could be improved, even if the price is reasonable · Because the resort is far from Ao Nang's restaurant area, heading out for every meal is less convenient than at a hotel in the town centre, so you rely on the shuttle or call a ride · Many people therefore choose to eat at the resort for some meals for convenience, or plan their main meal for when they are down at Ao Nang Beach anyway, where there are plenty of restaurants and seafood spots to choose from · One of the charms is sitting down to a quiet breakfast in the garden, listening to birdsong and looking at the cliff views — an atmosphere you will not get at a hotel in a busy area · Overall, food is not a reason to come to Vipa, but it is a decent extra, and you should set your expectations around convenience and atmosphere rather than menu variety

Service — service is the most strongly and consistently praised point in Vipa's real reviews · Many guests say the same thing: the staff are very friendly, help with everything, and give that warm family-stay feeling — from arranging island tours, booking cars and recommending restaurants, to handling the beach shuttle · One review describes finding the room not quite ready at check-in, but the team sorted it out quickly and well, which shows that even though the resort is small and resources are limited, the commitment to looking after guests is high · Being a small resort turns into an advantage, because the staff remember guests and look after them closely, rather than the queue-up service of a big hotel · The one thing to note is the lack of a 24-hour front desk, so if you arrive late or have something urgent at night you may need to contact them ahead · Overall, service is the strength that brings people back and gets them recommending it

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling together Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the beautiful, calm cliffside tropical garden, bungalows that are bigger than the price suggests and feel like a private house, friendly and very helpful staff, the free beach shuttle that solves the distance, a quiet and private pool, and good value among small properties · Many call it a "quiet oasis" that lets them genuinely relax away from the bustle · On the watch-out side: the most talked-about issue is the distance to the beach — about 2 kilometres, a long walk in the heat, so you depend on the shuttle and plan around its runs · After that come the plain breakfast with few choices, furniture and beds in some units starting to age (plus the odd well-used set of sheets), Wi-Fi that is slow in spots, and limited facilities with no 24-hour front desk or gym · Most of these gripes are about "setting your expectations right" for a small garden resort away from the beach, rather than problems that make people regret staying

"The bungalow was much bigger than I expected — paying this price for this much space is good value, and the garden is lovely and shady, great for photos · The only downside is the breakfast is a bit plain, and you have to wait for the scheduled shuttle to get down to the beach."

Price and value — the Standard Room starts at around THB 1,300/night (about US$39) at normal rates, and can climb in high season or over long weekends · Bigger rooms like the Superior Triple and the One/Two-Bedroom Villa bungalows fall in the range of about THB 1,800 up to around THB 3,000+ depending on size and timing · Compared with hotels and resorts in Ao Nang that sit on the beach or in the middle of the restaurant area — which usually start higher and have smaller rooms — Vipa feels very good value in terms of space for the money, especially if you choose a separate bungalow as spacious as a little house in the garden · The money you "pay less because you are away from the beach" is what you trade for quiet, trees and space · If you plan to use Krabi as a base for island tours by day and come back to sleep somewhere quiet at night, this price gives you full value · But if you put a premium on being able to walk to the beach and restaurants any time, the extra you pay for a hotel in the heart of the area may be worth more to you

Good to know before you book — a few things make the stay smoother · One, understand the location clearly: the resort is not beachfront, about 2 kilometres away, and plan to use the free beach shuttle on its schedule — ask for the shuttle timetable at check-in so you can build your day around it · Two, if you are coming as a group or family, choose a One/Two-Bedroom Villa, which is more spacious and better value than booking several rooms · Three, check the room, bed and sheets the moment you arrive, and if you find anything old or not clean, tell the team and ask to switch or fix it — reviews say the staff handle this well · Four, if you need the internet seriously, bring a backup mobile data SIM in case the Wi-Fi is slow · Five, since there is no 24-hour front desk, if you arrive late, let them know your check-in time and book the airport transfer ahead · Six, in Krabi's high season (November–April), places fill fast and prices rise, so book ahead and choose free cancellation while your plans are still uncertain

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Vipa Tropical Resort is the best fit for people who come to Krabi and value quiet, nature and spacious rooms at an easy price over being right by the beach · The shady cliffside tropical garden, bungalows as spacious as a private house, attentive staff and the free beach shuttle make it a quiet oasis with good value among Ao Nang's small properties · But if you want to step out of the room straight onto the beach or restaurants, want the full facilities of a big hotel, or want every corner of the room brand new, this may not be the answer, and you should look at a hotel right in the Ao Nang beach area instead · For a relaxing trip where you want to escape the bustle, use the resort as a quiet base, head out to sea by day and come back to sleep in the garden — Vipa answers that need well at an affordable price, and that is why it still scores highly and keeps getting recommended

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Vipa Tropical Resort Krabi

faq.q: Where is Vipa Tropical Resort · is it far from Ao Nang Beach?
faq.a: It sits in the Ao Nang area of Mueang Krabi, in a tropical garden below the limestone cliffs · It is not beachfront, about 2 kilometres from Ao Nang Beach (around a 25-minute walk), but there is a free beach shuttle several times a day · It is about 25 km from Krabi Airport (KBV), or a 30–40 min drive · It suits people who want to stay somewhere quiet and use the shuttle down to the beach

faq.q: What is the starting price at Vipa Tropical Resort · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,300/night (about US$39) for a Standard Room · There is a Superior Triple Room for 3 people, plus separate One-Bedroom Villa and Two-Bedroom Villa bungalows for families and groups · Prices depend on the season, rising in high season (Nov–Apr), so it is worth comparing several platforms and booking ahead

faq.q: Who is Vipa Tropical Resort for?
faq.a: It is a great fit for couples, families and travellers who value quiet, nature and spacious rooms at an easy price over being right by the beach · You get a spacious garden bungalow, a quiet atmosphere and attentive staff · It is less suited to people who want to step out of the room straight onto the beach and restaurants, or who want the full facilities of a big hotel

faq.q: What is the beach shuttle at Vipa Tropical Resort like?
faq.a: The resort runs a free beach shuttle several times a day, going in and out of the Ao Nang beach area on a set schedule, which many reviews praise for solving the distance well · It is best to ask for the shuttle timetable at check-in so you can plan your day around the runs · If you miss a run, you can call a taxi or motorbike taxi (for a fee)

faq.q: Does Vipa Tropical Resort have breakfast and a pool?
faq.a: There is an outdoor pool ringed by garden and cliff views, with a quiet, private feel · There is an on-site restaurant serving Thai food and simple dishes, plus breakfast · Reviews on breakfast are fairly mixed, with many saying it is plain with not many choices, even if the price is reasonable · Since it is far from the restaurant area, it is worth planning some meals for when you are down at the beach too

faq.q: How far ahead should you book · can you cancel?
faq.a: In Krabi's high season (November–April) you should book 3–6 weeks ahead, since it is a small property with just 17 units/rooms that fills fast, especially the villa bungalows · Every platform usually has a Free Cancellation option — choose that up front if your plans are still uncertain, or in case you need to change rooms at check-in
